title: Developer
summary: For software developers: projects first, the stack you work in, talks and writing, and where to find your code.

notFor: Developers looking for a job right now (start from job-seeker)

cards.purpose: Three to six projects they want to be known for.
What they work in and what they are learning.
Optional: how to reach them for work.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a square photo or logo for your profile picture?
slots.write: The member uploads it in the editor; never fetch one from the web.

slots.ask: Which three to six projects do you want to be known for? Paste their links.
slots.write: tag = main language · licence; title = the project name; description = what it does in one line, from the project's own README if they agree.

slots.ask: What do you work in day to day, what are you comfortable with, and what are you learning?
slots.write: Bold-labelled lines as in the sample; no skill ratings or percentages.

slots.ask: Do you want people to contact you about work? If so, how?
slots.write: Heading = their availability in a few words. Email: Only an address they confirm may be public: everyone can see it.

slots.ask: Any talks or posts you want to list?
slots.write: tag = Talk or Post · year; title = the published title; description = event and city for talks.

slots.ask: Where is your code, and which other accounts should be linked?
slots.write: Account URLs only; the app shows the site and account name.
